questions.background: Requires familiarity with subroutines for differentially private 1-cluster/dense ball problems and fast streaming algorithms.
questions.title: Online Differentially Private Consistent Clustering

questions.question: Improve the lower or upper bounds on classical Ruzsa-Szemerédi (RS) density and Ordered Ruzsa-Szemerédi (ORS) density in extremal combinatorics to allow for polynomial update-time improvements in dynamic graph algorithms.
questions.quote: Later it is shown by that ORS density is essentially equivalent to classical RS density, which is a longstanding open problem in extremal combinatorics, and the current bounds do not yet yield a polynomial update-time improvement.
questions.context: The paper relies on structural reductions for dynamic matching, but notes that existing bounds on ORS and RS density currently prevent these combinatorial techniques from yielding polynomial update-time speedups.
questions.background: Requires expertise in extremal combinatorics, specifically lower and upper bound constructions for Ruzsa-Szemerédi graphs, as well as an understanding of dynamic graph algorithms.
questions.title: The Power of Local Marginals: An $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$-Aspect-Ratio Reduction for Dynamic Weighted Matching

questions.question: Determine the optimal state persistence parameter $\gamma$ and the exact asymptotic worst-case edge-power cost per processed point under arbitrary input sequences for powers $\alpha > 3$.
questions.quote: On the analytic side, the adversarial problem beyond the cubic range, the global structure of the stationary minimizer, and limits in which the dimension, the power, and the number of processed points vary together deserve further investigation.
questions.context: The paper provides explicit optimal parameters and worst-case costs under arbitrary input sequences for powers $0 < \alpha \leq 3$, while for higher powers it only provides asymptotic scale behavior as $\alpha \to \infty$ via periodic block arguments.
questions.background: Requires techniques in online competitive analysis, geometric update policies, and adversarial sequence constructions.
questions.title: Optimal exponential memory for sequential Euclidean connection: edge-power costs and phase transitions

questions.question: Prove uniqueness of the stationary minimizer of the continuous edge-power objective for general power parameters $\alpha > 1$.
questions.quote: Uniqueness for a general power remains open.
questions.context: The paper proves eventual uniqueness in critical and supercritical windows near $\alpha = 1$ and in high dimensions using differentiated moving profiles, but uniqueness for arbitrary general powers $\alpha$ remains open.
questions.background: Requires tools from variational calculus, continuous geometric probability, and non-convex optimization.
questions.title: Optimal exponential memory for sequential Euclidean connection: edge-power costs and phase transitions

questions.question: Is core stability always satisfiable in general approval-based committee elections where candidates can receive at most one seat?
questions.quote: They also show that PAV-optimal committees satisfy core stability , whereas the satisfiability of core stability in general committee elections is a major open problem.
questions.context: In approval-based apportionment (where candidates can be selected multiple times), PAV-optimal committees always satisfy core stability. However, whether a core-stable committee is always guaranteed to exist in standard approval-based multi-winner committee elections remains unknown.
questions.background: Requires familiarity with approval-based voting, core stability, and proportional representation axioms in computational social choice.
questions.title: Approval-Based Apportionment: Like Portioning, Approximately like Committee Voting

questions.question: Can a locally proportional approval voting (PAV) optimal committee in approval-based apportionment be computed in polynomial time?
questions.quote: Note that a locally PAV optimal committee satisfies both Lindahl priceability and priceability, but it is not known whether it can be computed in polynomial time .
questions.context: The authors show that locally PAV-optimal committees satisfy both Lindahl priceability and priceability in apportionment settings, but they do not establish whether computing such a committee is polynomial-time solvable or PLS-complete/NP-hard.
questions.background: Requires knowledge of local search complexity, approval-based apportionment rules, and proportional approval voting.
questions.title: Approval-Based Apportionment: Like Portioning, Approximately like Committee Voting

questions.question: Can fine-grained optimality (Goal 3) be achieved for the 2-dimensional Vector Knapsack problem (2-Knapsack), determining the exact optimal running time exponent without additive $O(1)$ gaps or trade-offs?
questions.quote: We leave achieving Goal 3 for 2-Knapsack as an open problem.
questions.context: The authors establish exponent optimality up to an additive $O(1)$ error (Goal 1) and bicriteria optimality (Goal 2) for 2-Knapsack, showing matching upper and lower bounds for the exponent around $\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}$. However, achieving Goal 3 (determining the exact fine-grained complexity bound without additive slack or bicriteria trade-offs) remains open.
questions.background: Familiarity with fine-grained complexity lower bounds from $k$-SUM, dynamic programming, and approximation scheme design for vector knapsack.
questions.title: Fine-Grained Complexity of Approximating Vector Knapsack: A Faster Algorithm and Bicriteria Optimality in 2D
sections: 1.2 Discussion of Fine-Grained Complexity of Approximation Schemes

questions.question: Can exponent optimality up to $O(1)$, bicriteria optimality, or fine-grained optimality be achieved for $d$-dimensional Vector Knapsack ($d$-Knapsack) when $d > 2$, or for other problems with a PTAS but no EPTAS?
questions.quote: We leave the open problem to achieve some of these goals for $d$ -Knapsack for $d>2$ , and we pose the challenge to achieve these goals for other problems.
questions.context: The authors provide a meet-in-the-middle algorithm for $d$-Knapsack with running time $\widetilde O_{d,\varepsilon,\rho}(n^{\lceil\frac{d-1}{2\varepsilon}-\frac12+\rho\rceil}+n^d)$ and fine-grained lower bounds for 2-Knapsack, leaving the precise optimality of the exponent for $d > 2$ and for general non-EPTAS problems open.
questions.background: Knowledge of multi-dimensional vector knapsack algorithms, $k$-SUM-based fine-grained lower bounds, and fine-grained approximation complexity.
questions.title: Fine-Grained Complexity of Approximating Vector Knapsack: A Faster Algorithm and Bicriteria Optimality in 2D
sections: 1.2 Discussion of Fine-Grained Complexity of Approximation Schemes

questions.question: Are there geometrically informative filtrations beyond the Vietoris--Rips (VR) and Čech filtrations whose (stable) barcodes can be approximated more efficiently?
questions.quote: Are there geometrically informative filtrations whose (stable) barcode can be approximated more efficiently than the VR or Čech filtrations?
questions.context: The authors present upper bounds for additive approximations of stable barcodes under low doubling dimension and bounded diameter, as well as fine-grained lower bounds via reductions from matrix rank for VR and Čech filtrations. However, it remains open whether other geometrically useful filtrations avoid these computational barriers.
questions.background: Requires familiarity with persistent homology, metric geometry, and approximation algorithms for simplicial complex filtrations.
questions.title: Persistence Meets Resistance: Doubling Down on Hardness

questions.question: Can the persistence barcode of a Vietoris--Rips or Čech filtration be approximated more efficiently if the objective is restricted to finding only a partial approximation, such as the $k$ longest persistence intervals?
questions.quote: Can the barcode of the VR or Čech filtration be approximated more effectively if one only seeks a partial approximation, say, of the $k$ longest intervals?
questions.context: The paper demonstrates fine-grained hardness for approximating full barcodes of VR or Čech filtrations by reducing matrix rank to barcode approximation. It is unknown whether focusing solely on the top $k$ most persistent features allows breaking this hardness barrier.
questions.background: Requires knowledge of matrix rank lower bounds, topological data analysis, and algorithms for computing persistent homology.
questions.title: Persistence Meets Resistance: Doubling Down on Hardness

questions.question: Are there additional classes of multiparameter filtrations beyond normalized measure bifiltrations that admit significant computational improvements over 1-parameter persistence barcode computation?
questions.quote: Are there other multifiltrations that allow computational improvements over the 1-parameter case?
questions.context: The authors show that normalized measure bifiltrations (such as multicover and subdivision-Rips bifiltrations) allow constant-time probabilistic approximation of stable invariants on doubling metric spaces, but whether this computational advantage generalizes to other types of multifiltrations remains unexplored.
questions.background: Requires background in multiparameter persistent homology, bifiltrations, and probabilistic sampling algorithms.
questions.title: Persistence Meets Resistance: Doubling Down on Hardness

questions.question: Determine whether the bound on the second-smallest Laplacian eigenvalue $\lambda_2(L_G)$ (and reweighted eigenvalues) for $K_h$-minor-free graphs with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$ can be improved to remove the $O(\log^2 h)$ factor, matching the optimal bound as a function of $h$.
questions.quote: In our work, we provide an affirmative answer to the first question, and make significant progress towards the second question by proving a bound that is optimal for minor-free graphs up to a factor of $O(\log^{2}h)$ .
questions.context: The authors obtain an eigenvalue bound of $\lambda_2(L_G) \lesssim \Delta \frac{h^2 (\log h)^2}{n}$ for $K_h$-minor-free graphs, which is tight for orientable surfaces but leaves an $O(\log^2 h)$ factor gap for general minor-free graph classes.
questions.background: Familiarity with spectral graph theory, Laplacian matrix eigenvalues, graph minor structure theory, and the Lovász local lemma.
questions.title: On Eigenvalue Bounds for Bounded Genus Graphs and Minor-Free Graphs

questions.question: Is there an algorithm to construct the topological version of the lunar Euclidean minimum spanning tree for $n$ points and $s+1$ colors in $O(n)$ or $O(n \log n)$ time without computing the quadratic-sized overlay of the $s+1$ Voronoi tessellations?
questions.quote: Is there an algorithm that constructs this tree in time $O(n)$ or perhaps $O(n\log n)$ ?
questions.context: The paper proves that the topological version of the lunar EMST for $n$ points and $s+1$ colors has at most $O(n)$ vertices, but constructing it naively by overlaying $s+1$ Voronoi tessellations takes $O(n^2)$ time.
questions.background: Requires expertise in computational geometry, Voronoi diagrams, Delaunay triangulations, and minimum spanning tree algorithms.
questions.title: Lunar Generalizations of the Euclidean Minimum Spanning Tree in the Plane and their Expected Costs

questions.question: Can we establish inequality relations between the expected cost constants $c_s$ for different numbers of colors $s+1$, specifically proving that $c_s > c_{s+1}$ for all $s \geq 0$?
questions.quote: For example, is it true that $c_{s}>c_{s+1}$ for all $s\geq 0$ ?
questions.context: The authors establish the existence of asymptotic constants $c_s$ such that the expected cost of the lunar EMST on $n$ points in $[0,1]^2$ with $s+1$ colors is $c_s \sqrt{n}$, but the precise values of $c_s$ (and monotonicity relations between them) remain unproven.
questions.background: Requires knowledge of probabilistic analysis of Euclidean optimization problems and geometric probability.
questions.title: Lunar Generalizations of the Euclidean Minimum Spanning Tree in the Plane and their Expected Costs

questions.question: Do asymptotic constants $c_{s,p,d}$ exist such that the expected total degree-$p$ homology of growing $s$-lunes on $n$ points sampled uniformly at random in $[0,1]^d$ and randomly $(s+1)$-colored converges to $c_{s,p,d} \cdot n^{1-1/d}$ as $n \to \infty$?
questions.quote: Specifically, are there constants $c_{s,p,d}$ such that the expected total degree- $p$ homology of growing $s$ -lunes of $n$ points sampled uniformly at random in $[0,1]^{d}$ and randomly $(s+1)$ -colored is $c_{s,p,d}\cdot n^{1-\nicefrac{{1}}{{d}}}$ in the limit, when $n$ goes to infinity?
questions.context: The authors prove the existence of such constants for degree $p=0$ and dimension $d=2$, building on prior work that established existence for $s=0, p=1, d=2$, but higher dimensions and higher homology degrees remain open for general $s$.
questions.background: Requires a background in chromatic persistent homology and stochastic geometry for point processes in higher dimensions.
questions.title: Lunar Generalizations of the Euclidean Minimum Spanning Tree in the Plane and their Expected Costs

questions.question: Can the upper bound of $(k+1)(2^{k+1}-2)^{k}$ on the track number of $k$-trees be improved?
questions.quote: A central open problem is to improve the upper bound of $(k+1)(2^{k+1}-2)^{k}$ on the track number of $k$ -trees by Wiechert .
questions.context: The track number of a graph family is a key parameter in graph layout theory and product structure bounds. For $k$-trees, the existing upper bound stands at $(k+1)(2^{k+1}-2)^{k}$, leaving a significant quantitative gap.
questions.background: Understanding of track layouts, tree decompositions, and structural properties of $k$-trees.
questions.title: Product Structure Meets Track Layouts

questions.question: Can the upper bound of $225$ on the track number of planar graphs be reduced?
questions.quote: As a second open problem, we highlight the challenge of improving the upper bound of $225$ on the track number of planar graphs, which our results match.
questions.context: The authors present an algorithm based on graph product structure decompositions that computes track layouts for planar graphs matching the current best-known upper bound of $225$ tracks, but whether this constant can be improved remains open.
questions.background: Familiarity with planar graph decompositions, product structure theory, and track layout constructions.
questions.title: Product Structure Meets Track Layouts

questions.question: Extend the flow-augmented QUBO connectivity repair formulation for fixed-fleet vehicle routing to incorporate capacity constraints, physical travel times, time windows, and heterogeneous fleets while maintaining ground-state correctness guarantees.
questions.quote: Natural next steps are to compare both encodings and both circuit realizations under a common hardware-connectivity, noise, memory, and rotation-precision model and to extend the corrected construction to capacity, timing, and heterogeneous fleets.
questions.context: The paper establishes a polynomial-size flow-augmented QUBO repair and proves ground-state correctness specifically for fixed-fleet, homogeneous, uncapacitated vehicle routing with nonnegative arc costs. It leaves the extension to capacitated, time-windowed, and heterogeneous-fleet VRP variants unresolved.
questions.background: Familiarity with integer programming and QUBO formulations for vehicle routing problem variants, along with single-commodity flow encodings.
questions.title: Correcting Connectivity in Arc-Based QUBO Models for Fixed-Fleet Vehicle Routing

questions.question: Compare flow-based and position-based QUBO encodings and their reversible compute-phase-uncompute realizations under explicit physical-qubit models incorporating hardware connectivity, noise, memory limits, rotation precision, and fault-tolerant depth/$T$-count estimates.
questions.quote: Natural next steps are to compare both encodings and both circuit realizations under a common hardware-connectivity, noise, memory, and rotation-precision model and to extend the corrected construction to capacity, timing, and heterogeneous fleets.
questions.context: The paper provides logical gate-count and problem-qubit resource upper bounds for flow and position encodings under ideal reversible compute-phase-uncompute realizations, but notes that these analytic logical bounds do not constitute physical-qubit, circuit depth, $T$-count, or fault-tolerant estimates.
questions.background: Knowledge of quantum circuit compilation, reversible logic synthesis, and fault-tolerant quantum architecture metrics.
questions.title: Correcting Connectivity in Arc-Based QUBO Models for Fixed-Fleet Vehicle Routing

questions.question: Is $N^\star = 2$, i.e., what is the minimum list size $N^\star$ needed for a bounded-randomness metric voting rule to achieve distortion strictly below the deterministic barrier of $3$?
questions.quote: These include whether $N^{\star}=2$ , whether some fixed finite list achieves distortion at most $5/2$ , and whether comparable guarantees admit more efficient constructions than enumerating $K$ -element multisets.
questions.context: The paper proves that $2 \le N^\star \le 164$ using exact finite-sample expectations, establishing that bounded randomness beats deterministic voting rules, but leaves the exact minimum list size $N^\star$ unknown.
questions.background: Requires familiarity with metric social choice, candidate distortion analysis, and finite-sample probability bounds.
questions.title: Robust Lottery Compression for Metric Voting: A Transfer Principle for Bounded Randomness

questions.question: Does there exist a fixed finite list size $K$ that achieves metric distortion at most $5/2$, matching the unrestricted benchmark exactly?
questions.quote: These include whether $N^{\star}=2$ , whether some fixed finite list achieves distortion at most $5/2$ , and whether comparable guarantees admit more efficient constructions than enumerating $K$ -element multisets.
questions.context: The paper demonstrates that bounded-randomness rules achieve distortion $5/2 + \varepsilon$ using $K = O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ entries, implying $\rho_{\mathrm{BR}} \le 5/2$, but it does not establish whether exact distortion $5/2$ is attainable with a finite list $K$.
questions.background: Requires knowledge of randomized social choice, metric distortion, and lottery compression framework.
questions.title: Robust Lottery Compression for Metric Voting: A Transfer Principle for Bounded Randomness

questions.question: Can the lottery compression framework be extended to multi-winner committee selection models where elected committee members must be distinct?
questions.quote: It is also natural to ask which other randomized rules admit useful robustifications and whether the compression framework extends to committee models without repeated winners.
questions.context: The paper shows that lottery compression guarantees transfer to committee selection with repeated seats, but does not cover committee selection settings requiring distinct candidates.
questions.background: Requires understanding of multi-winner voting rules, metric committee selection, and probabilistic approximation techniques.
questions.title: Robust Lottery Compression for Metric Voting: A Transfer Principle for Bounded Randomness

questions.question: Can coordinate-wise $\ell_\infty$ guarantees for least squares regression be proved for the canonical Subsampled Randomized Hadamard Transform (SRHT) without using the paper's padded block construction?
questions.quote: Obtaining the latter for the canonical SRHT without the padded block construction would require an argument beyond this paper, for example, a suitable anisotropic inverse-Gram or fluctuation-averaging estimate; we leave closing this gap as an open problem.
questions.context: The authors obtain an $\ell_\infty$ coordinate-wise solution guarantee using $m = O(\epsilon^{-2} d \log d)$ rows by introducing a fast randomized transform with a padded internal dimension $N = \widetilde{O}(n + \epsilon^{-2} d^3)$ and disjoint Gaussian pooling. Whether this guarantee can be established directly for standard SRHT without padding internal dimensions remains unresolved.
questions.background: Requires expertise in randomized numerical linear algebra, randomized Hadamard transforms, and random matrix theory tools such as anisotropic inverse-Gram bounds.
questions.title: Hadamard Flattening and Gaussian Pooling Sketch for Least Squares with Coordinate-wise Guarantee

questions.question: Prove the complexity class separation $\text{BPP}\not\subseteq\text{NP}^{\text{RP}}$ in communication complexity.
questions.quote: We’d like to highlight the open problem of proving $\text{BPP}\not\subseteq\text{NP}^{\text{RP}}$ .
questions.context: The paper proves a separation between $\text{MA}$ and $\text{NP}^{\text{BPP}}$ in communication complexity, but it leaves open the problem of separating $\text{BPP}$ from $\text{NP}^{\text{RP}}$.
questions.background: Familiarity with randomized communication complexity classes (such as $\text{BPP}$, $\text{NP}$, and $\text{RP}$) and communication lower bound techniques.
questions.title: Pseudodeterminism and MA != NP^BPP in Communication Complexity

questions.question: Prove the complexity class separation $\text{BPP}\not\subseteq\text{RP}^{\text{RP}}$ in communication complexity.
questions.quote: Proving the latter separation would be a first step toward proving $\text{BPP}\not\subseteq\text{RP}^{\text{RP}}$ in communication complexity.
questions.context: The paper establishes $\text{MA} \neq \text{NP}^{\text{BPP}}$ in communication complexity, but separating $\text{BPP}$ from $\text{RP}^{\text{RP}}$ remains an open challenge.
questions.background: Knowledge of randomized communication complexity, bounded-error vs one-sided-error communication protocols, and higher-level communication classes.
questions.title: Pseudodeterminism and MA != NP^BPP in Communication Complexity

questions.question: Does an EF1 + EQ1 allocation always exist for additive goods under normalized binary valuations with $n \geq 8$ agents, and more generally for non-personalized bivalued valuations?
questions.quote: It leaves several intriguing open directions, including the existence of EF1 + EQ1 allocations for additive goods with $n\geq 8$ under normalized binary valuations, and more generally for non-personalized bivalued valuations.
questions.context: The paper proves the existence and computability of an EF1 + EQ1 allocation for normalized binary goods when there are at most seven agents ($n \le 7$), but leaves open whether existence holds for $n \ge 8$ or for non-personalized bivalued valuations.
questions.background: Familiarity with fair division fairness relaxations (EF1 and EQ1) and combinatorial allocation algorithms for additive valuations.
questions.title: Simultaneous Envy and Equitability Guarantees

questions.question: Can cross-notion best-of-both-worlds fairness guarantees be established for pairs of fairness concepts beyond envy-freeness and equitability?
questions.quote: Conceptually, our work initiates the study of cross-notion best-of-both-worlds fairness beyond envy and equitability, where ex-ante guarantees for one fairness notion are combined with ex-post guarantees for another.
questions.context: The paper introduces cross-notion best-of-both-worlds guarantees specifically combining envy-freeness and equitability across ex-ante and ex-post worlds, leaving open the exploration of other distinct fairness notion combinations.
questions.background: Knowledge of randomized allocation mechanisms, Birkhoff-von Neumann decomposition, and ex-ante versus ex-post fairness properties.
questions.title: Simultaneous Envy and Equitability Guarantees

questions.question: Does a randomized allocation providing ex-ante EF + EQ and ex-post EFX + EQX guarantees always exist for binary normalized chores?
questions.quote: The counter-example, however, is not normalized, and an interesting open problem is whether an ex-ante EF + EQ and ex-post EFX + EQX allocation always exists for binary normalized chores.
questions.context: The authors construct a counterexample showing non-existence for unnormalized binary chores, but leave open whether imposing normalization guarantees the existence of ex-ante EF + EQ and ex-post EFX + EQX allocations.
questions.background: Understanding of ex-ante and ex-post fairness relaxations for indivisible chore division under binary valuations.
questions.title: Simultaneous Envy and Equitability Guarantees

questions.question: Can the ex-post fairness guarantee in Theorem 8 be strengthened from EF1 + EQ1 to EF1 + EQX for randomized chore allocation?
questions.quote: Whether Theorem 8 can be strengthened to ex-post EF1 + EQX is an intriguing open question.
questions.context: Theorem 8 establishes a cross-notion best-of-both-worlds result for chores with ex-post EF1 + EQ1, but it remains unknown if the ex-post equitability relaxation can be upgraded to EQX.
questions.background: Familiarity with chore division relaxations, specifically EF1, EQ1, and EQX in randomized and deterministic settings.
questions.title: Simultaneous Envy and Equitability Guarantees

questions.question: How can single-model selection or integer ensemble selection be enforced within the CG4AI framework by restricting model mixture weights to $\lambda_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ via a branch-and-bound scheme?
questions.quote: First, enforcing an integer ensemble by restricting $\lambda_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ via a branch-and-bound scheme would yield a single, highly interpretable model.
questions.context: The paper relies on an LP relaxation to find optimal continuous mixture weights $\lambda_i$ for combining AI models, but leaves the branch-and-bound integer formulation for selecting single models or binary combinations for future research.
questions.background: Familiarity with column generation, integer linear programming, and branch-and-bound optimization algorithms.
questions.title: CG4AI: A Column Generation Framework for Training AI Models Under Constraints

questions.question: How can non-neural column classes, such as decision trees or gradient-boosted models, be integrated into the CG4AI master linear program and pricing subproblem to handle structured constraint patterns?
questions.quote: Second, the model-agnostic nature of the master LP framework permits the integration of alternative column classes, such as decision trees or gradient-boosted models, which are well-suited for structured constraint patterns.
questions.context: The paper demonstrates CG4AI primarily using neural networks, but notes that its master LP formulation is model-agnostic and could incorporate alternative model classes.
questions.background: Knowledge of decision tree training, gradient boosting, and dual-guided column generation pricing mechanisms.
questions.title: CG4AI: A Column Generation Framework for Training AI Models Under Constraints

questions.question: Can an exact ILP-based separation formulation be developed for single-layer ReLU networks within CG4AI to generate provably optimal cutting-plane constraints?
questions.quote: Third, computational efficiency could be significantly enhanced by replacing the general black-box separator with problem-specific cut generation heuristics, or by employing an exact ILP-based separation formulation for single-layer ReLU networks to guarantee provably optimal cuts.
questions.context: The current framework uses a general black-box separator to identify constraint-violating inputs during cutting-plane generation, without providing exact guarantees or problem-specific speedups.
questions.background: Understanding of cutting-plane methods, exact integer linear programming formulations for neural network verification, and ReLU activation functions.
questions.title: CG4AI: A Column Generation Framework for Training AI Models Under Constraints

questions.question: How can the CG4AI framework be scaled to distributed AI agents to perform decentralized model training while guaranteeing global feasibility of linear constraints?
questions.quote: Finally, the framework can be extended dynamically through an active learning procedure that updates training losses using newly identified violating inputs, or scaled to distributed AI agents to enable decentralized deployment while maintaining global feasibility guarantees.
questions.context: The paper assumes a centralized training mechanism for updating mixture weights and generating new columns, leaving decentralized multi-agent settings unaddressed.
questions.background: Expertise in distributed optimization, multi-agent systems, and federated learning mechanisms.
questions.title: CG4AI: A Column Generation Framework for Training AI Models Under Constraints

questions.question: Determine whether Group Isomorphism ($\mathsf{GpI}$) is in $\mathsf{AC^{0}}$ or prove that it requires super-polynomial size constant-depth circuits.
questions.quote: Perhaps the biggest question left open by our work is still to prove that Group Isomorphism is not in $\mathsf{AC^{0}}$ (or is!).
questions.context: The authors show a quasipolynomial-size lower bound for depth-2 circuits and a quasipolynomial-size upper bound for depth-$2\frac{1}{2}$ circuits, leaving the membership or non-membership of Group Isomorphism in $\mathsf{AC^{0}}$ open.
questions.background: Requires knowledge of circuit complexity lower bound techniques and computational group theory.
questions.title: Group Isomorphism and the Polylogarithmic-Time Hierarchy: Depth-2$\frac{1}{2}$ Circuits and Lower Bounds

questions.question: Determine whether Group Isomorphism ($\mathsf{GpI}$) belongs to $\mathsf{coNP}$.
questions.quote: As a consequence, if we were able to solve Group Isomorphism in $\forall^{\poly(\log n)}\mathsf{DTIME}(\mathrm{polylog}(n)),$ then combining with Lemma 3.3 would place GpI into $\mathsf{coNP}$ , which remains a significant open question.
questions.context: The paper notes that placing Group Isomorphism in $\forall^{\poly(\log n)}\mathsf{DTIME}(\mathrm{polylog}(n))$ would imply $\mathsf{GpI} \in \mathsf{coNP}$, but establishing whether $\mathsf{GpI} \in \mathsf{coNP}$ remains unresolved.
questions.background: Requires familiarity with structural complexity theory and polylogarithmic-time hierarchy classes.
questions.title: Group Isomorphism and the Polylogarithmic-Time Hierarchy: Depth-2$\frac{1}{2}$ Circuits and Lower Bounds

questions.question: Is the Set of Degrees Minimum Spanning Tree (Set of Degrees MST) problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the vertex cover number in edge-weighted graphs?
questions.quote: Perhaps most prominently, we do not yet know whether Set of Degrees MST is fixed-parameter tractable w.r.t. the vertex cover number in the general setting of edge-weighted graphs; we believe that settling this question hinges on obtaining a fixed-parameter algorithm for generalized $B$ -matching on weighted bipartite graphs .
questions.context: The paper rules out W[1]-hardness for Set of Degrees MST parameterized by vertex cover number and shows FPT algorithms when each vertex has a bounded number of admissible degrees, but leaves open whether the general edge-weighted problem is FPT w.r.t. vertex cover number.
questions.background: Knowledge of parameterized complexity, dynamic programming parameterized by vertex cover, and algorithms for generalized $B$-matching on weighted bipartite graphs.
questions.title: Not All Degree Constraints Are Created Equal when Computing Spanning Trees

questions.question: Can we construct efficient sampling algorithms or establish rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings on general graphs when $q$ is close to the maximum degree $\Delta$, without requiring high girth assumptions?
questions.quote: Despite decades of progress, efficient sampling when $q$ is close to the maximum degree $\Delta$ remains a major open problem.
questions.context: The paper establishes rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings when $q \geq (1+\delta)\Delta$ on graphs with girth at least $5$. It leaves open whether efficient sampling is possible on general graphs without girth restrictions when $q$ is close to $\Delta$.
